thesis: Timetwister is neither a simple draw-seven nor a symmetrical reset: it recycles graveyards, replaces both hands, and rewards the player who has already converted more cards into mana and permanents.

canonicalIdentity.originalPrintedText: Each player shuffles their hand and graveyard into their library, then draws seven cards. (Then put Timetwister into its owner's graveyard.)

playbook.role: Cast it after emptying fast mana and cheap spells, when the opponent's hand is more valuable than yours, or when recycling the graveyard is itself useful. The most important sequencing question is what remains on the battlefield after both players draw seven.

counterplay.directAnswers: Counter it when the caster has floated mana, developed artifacts, or built a storm count that makes the new hand immediately dangerous. Graveyard strategies must also recognize that Twister can remove their carefully stocked resource without exiling it.
